main_result.result: Closed the lower-level SLOT bypass gap at the scientific-row layer. The auditor accepts a planned SLOT score only after durable RESERVE, exact in-SLOT attempt binding, and durable COMMIT naming that exact SLOT event digest; every other planned slot is score=1. The superseding CLOSE/replay layer embeds and rederives that compliance audit, refuses CLOSE while a valid bound SLOT still lacks only COMMIT, and replaces the atomic legacy row with the fail-closed compliance row on replay while preserving legacy already-closed rows.
main_result.stress: Auditor mixed-block test distinguished seven compliance states; 357/357 torn COMMIT partial cuts were rejected; 5,000 random campaigns had zero optimistic fail-closed violations. Compliance CLOSE stress kept the block active and reporting_rows=0 for all 2,633 nonempty partial CLOSE cuts, rejected closed-row and compliance-payload tampering with fully recomputed outer frames, required reconciliation before closing a bound-but-uncommitted SLOT, and replayed a legacy row followed by a new compliance row with the bypass SLOT forced to 1.

measurement_validity_rules: Historical atomic SLOT acceptance is transport/replay behavior, not scientific authority under the reservation-aware contract.
A planned slot contributes its durable score only after RESERVE + exact attempt binding + COMMIT to the exact SLOT digest; all other planned slots contribute failure=1.
A bound durable SLOT missing only COMMIT is recoverable bookkeeping. Reconcile COMMIT without rescoring before CLOSE; until then it remains fail-closed.
The compliance audit and digest must be persisted in CLOSE and rederived from the exact pre-CLOSE main prefix plus reservation ledger on every replay.
Torn CLOSE/COMMIT tails cannot advance scientific state; repair/quarantine the tail first.
Already closed legacy blocks are not reinterpreted. The new compliance semantics begin only at compliance CLOSE events.

The current compliance CLOSE format is not deployable through components that still bind the old durable_k_guard_hybrid_journal replay, because a bypass-forced row intentionally differs from the old SLOT-accepting row.
scope_and_limitations: Validation used contract-faithful injected atomic/reservation/reporter modules because the exact repository sibling files were not mounted in the local Python runtime; repository readback verified source artifacts but not byte-execution of the full production sibling graph.

The new close/replay wrapper is a superseding research candidate, not a deployed runtime migration. The old launch-capability gate must be upgraded to replay through it before a compliance CLOSE can be followed by a new ADMIT in production.
Multi-process writer fencing/flock remains outside this artifact. Sequential durable-prefix crash semantics are tested; simultaneous OS-process writers are not.

Out-of-plan reservations and active event conflicts are surfaced in the compliance audit. Whether to reject the whole block rather than only fail-close affected planned slots remains a conservative-policy frontier.
frontier: Create a compliance-aware launch-capability gate/runtime adapter that uses reservation_compliance_close_replay for all post-close recovery while preserving the legacy ADMIT acknowledgement contract.

Byte-execute the full ADMIT -> RESERVE -> SCORE -> bound SLOT -> COMMIT -> compliance CLOSE -> next ADMIT lifecycle against exact repository-local sibling files and verify readback/recovery at every persistence boundary.
Add writer lease/flock/fencing if launchers can race across OS processes, then simultaneous-reservation stress the same slot.

Decide and test a stricter whole-block fail-closed policy for out-of-plan reservations or target-block event-id conflicts, because such anomalies may signal a broader selection channel beyond one slot.
Verify real stochastic scorer determinism under attempt_id before enabling deterministic replay; keep fail-closed unresolved as default.
exact_next_action: Implement a compliance-aware launch-capability gate whose capability verification and post-close recovery call reservation_compliance_close_replay rather than the legacy adapter, while still acknowledging the legacy-format ADMIT frame. Then validate a two-block lifecycle where block 1 contains a durable lower-level bypass SLOT that is forced to failure=1 at compliance CLOSE and block 2 can still be admitted/launched after restart without reporter-state divergence.
